summary: The Contender (#1185): the planning bot as one named configuration, BotContext.Contender(), registered as tournament arm 'contender' (all flags off by default; the champion and the practice opponent are unchanged). It keeps the purchase slate (Gold shape, bodies, Proclaim, clear-the-row) and triage's target ranking and printed-abilities-first ordering; the attack estimate, interview discard rule, Gold reserve and won-battle cap are off behind their own switches and arms (contender+attack/+discard/+reserve/+woncap/+all). Adds tools/bots/merge_tournament.py (pool reports from two machines), tools/bots/compare_tournament.py (paired comparison against the champion's own baseline on the same games), docs/bots/CONTENDER.md and a pre-registration note.
validation: bash tools/check.sh --skip-client passed (all shards). AI tests planner (5) and triage (2) pass. Contender arm, 364 games on seed block 1700: 0 stalls/illegal/exceptions; paired against the champion A/A baseline on the same games it gained 37 and lost 41 (net -4, p=0.73): neutral. Paired ablations on the same block: attack estimate about -14, interview discard rule about -11, reserve 0, won-battle cap -3, purchase slate -2, triage targets +1, printed-first +2. Merge tools exercised on existing reports.
remaining: The Contender is NOT better than the champion; nothing is promoted and the pre-registered decisive run (docs/bots/experiments/2026-11-07-contender.md, 2,184 games per arm) is not run. The attack estimate and discard rule lose games and need diagnosis; Action-phase sequencing, contingency branches, mitigation order and post-battle re-planning are not built; spent-ability memory only sees battle actions. Single-run win rates against 50% are misleading (the champion A/A scored 46.4% on block 1700): use compare_tournament.py.
